title: French forest understory plants shifted to warmer-climate species at about 28% of the rate of local warming in 2005-2022, at a constant rate that did not follow 5-year temperature changes
abstract: Question: did the understory flora of French forests change toward species of warmer climates in 2005-2022, which fraction of its own spatial temperature gradient did it follow, and did it respond to 5-year temperature or drought changes? Data: IGN National Forest Inventory floristic relevés (GBIF France, CC BY 4.0): 111,758 relevés, 2,548 understory species, 94,837 first visits and 16,443 plots surveyed again after about 5 years; E-OBS v31.0e climate; EIVE 1.0 indicator values. Method: a plan written before the outcome models; cross-fitted species temperature indices from 1991-2020 site temperature; floristic temperature (FT) per relevé; repeated cross-sections with 0.25-degree cell fixed effects and survey-month, soil and canopy controls; within-plot change between revisits; errors clustered on 93 one-degree blocks and block bootstrap. Results: FT increased 0.277 C per 1 C of site temperature in space. In first visits FT increased 0.036 C per decade (95% CI 0.026-0.046), 0.28 (bootstrap 0.22-0.34) of the change that full tracking of the local 5-year mean temperature predicts; it increased in all four regions (fractions 0.20-0.54). The rate was the same in 2005-2013, when 5-year temperatures fell, and in 2014-2022, when they rose fast. In revisits FT increased 0.017 C in 5 years (fraction 0.18, 0.10-0.31) and did not depend on the warming between visits (fast fraction -0.02, -0.10 to 0.06). Drought and heat summers had no detectable effect; canopy loss raised FT. Losses of cold-affiliated and gains of warm-affiliated species made the shift; gains of cold-affiliated tree seedlings and losses of Atlantic heath species partly cancelled it. EIVE nitrogen also increased, but not steadily (it fell in 2020-2022). Observation bias: winter relevés had FT 0.12 C higher than July relevés of the same cells, and the places of first-visit plots changed between years, which gives steps in naive annual means as large as the climate signal. Conclusion: the understory thermophilized slowly and at a constant rate, not as a fast response to recent weather. Limitations: grid temperature without plot elevation, correlational design, no deposition or management data.
